texts.preamble: Abhishek vs Gopal Singh Rawat on 12 November, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Cnr No.DLSE01-006324-2018 1. Abhishek S/o Sh. Sughar Singh R/o B1-287A-1, Gali no.11, New Ashok Nagar, Vasundhra Enclave, Delhi. ....Claimants/Petitioners Versus 1. Gopal Singh Rawat S/o Sh. Bheem Singh Rawat R/o Village Gudalivia, Post Shrinagar, Ajmer Rajasthan-209286. ....Driver cum owner/Respondent no.1 2. National Insurance Company Ltd. Office at: Building no.58, 302-304, 3rd Floor Sahyog Building, Nehru place, New Delhi. ....Insurance company/Respondent no.2 Date of accident : 25.01.2018 Result of accident : Grievous Injury Mact no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Page no. 1 of 23 ss (permanent disability) Date of filing of petition : 11.07.2018 Date of Decision : 12.11.2025 Award 1.
texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one minor, master Abhishek Kumar, aged about 7 years, sustained grievous injury resulting in permanent disability. An application u/s 166 (1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant through his legal guardian. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 25.01.2018, at about 5:30 -06:00 p.m., master Abhishek along with one Gautam Kumar (aged about 15 years), were returning from tuition classes on motorcycle bearing no.UP16-BF-3076, which was driven by one Neeraj. When their motorcycle reached Havert Company crossing, a speeding truck bearing no.RJ-01GA-9045 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle), hit the motorcycle causing Abhishek vs Gopal Singh Rawat on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149378006/ 1 severe injury to victim Gautam Kumar leading to his death on the spot while causing grievous head injury to Abhishek. While victim Gautam Kumar died on the spot, victim Abhishek was rushed to hospital for treatment. Separate claim petitions were filed seeking compensation qua death of victim Gautam Kumar and the present one, seeking compensation qua injury resulting in disability caused to victim Gautam Kumar. The claim relating to victim Abhishek is separately registered with MACT No.668/2018, titled as Ranjeet Kumar vs. Gopal Singh Rawat. 3. An FIR No.0081/18, dated 25.01.2018 u/s 279,338,304A IPC was registered at PS Surajpur, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P. MACT no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Page no. 2 of 23 ss Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet before concerned criminal court. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was being driven and owned by respondent no.1 and insured with respondent no. 2/Insurance company. 5. In response to the petition, respondent no.1 filed his reply denying the averment of rash and negligent driving by him. It has been stated in the reply that the accident, if any, took place due to negligence of the driver of the motorcycle on which victim was riding. It is pleaded that the victim was triple riding on the motorcycle without a helmet at a high speed and in violation of the traffic norms and struck his motorcycle from the service lane into the trolla driven by respondent no.1. Liability to compensate is further denied on the ground that the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.2. Respondent no.2 also filed its reply denying liability on the ground that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased who was triple riding on the motorcycle and the motorcycle was being driven by its driver without a valid driving licence. It has been pleaded that since the accident was a head on collision, contributory negligence of the motorcycle on which victim was riding is implicit. Respondent no.2 has also challenged the jurisdiction of this Tribunal. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 03.01.2019. OPP. 4) Relief. 7. In order to prove his claim, petitioner examined Sh. Sughar Singh (father of petitioner) as PW-1 and one Neeraj Kumar (driver of the motorcycle bearing no. UP-16BF-3076 and eye witness) as Abhishek vs Gopal Singh Rawat on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149378006/ 2 PW-2. PW-1/petitioner no.1 tendered his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW-1/A, wherein he stated that he is father of petitioner Abhishk, who suffered grievous injuries in a road accident on 25.01.2018, at about 05:30-06:00 p.m, in front of Havert Company crossing, PS Surajpur Gautam Budh Nagar,U.P. He relied upon his Adhar card as Ex.PW1/1. He deposed that on 25.01.2018 his son Abhishek along with friend Gautam Kumar, was returning from tuition class on motorcycle bearing no.UP-16BF-3076 which was being driven by Neeraj. At about 5:30-6:00 p.m, on reaching the road in front of Havert Company crossing, a speeding truck bearing no.RJ-01GA-9045 suddenly came and hit the motorcycle causing grievous injuries to Abhishek. The other occupant of the motorcycle was crushed under the wheels of the truck resulting in his death on the spot. Injured petitioner was rushed to Green City Hospital from where he was discharged on 26.01.2018 and referred to Safdarjung Hospital. He remained under treatment at Safdarjung Hospital till 31.01.2018. He was again admitted on 02.03.2018 and remained hospitalized till 07.03.2018. He deposed that the victim has developed severe mental issues such MACT no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Page no. 4 of 23 ss as fits and speech disorder. He relied upon the medical record as Ex.PW1/2 and PW1/3. Medical bills are Ex.PW1/4 and certificate issued by Bharti Public School as Ex.PW1/5. It is further deposed that the victim was a student of class 2 nd and had to drop out of the school due to the disability suffered by him in the accident. PW-1 was duly cross examined by learned counsel for insurance company. 8. Sh. Neeraj Kumar was examined as PW-2 who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW2/A and deposed that on 25.01.2018, he along with Gautam Kumar and his brother Abhishek were traveling on motorcycle bearing no.UP16BF-3076 which was being driven by him. At about 05:30-06:00 p.m, on reaching in front of Havert Company crossing, he was going toward company no. D-9, Surajpur. The traffic signal on his side was green and therefore he was crossing the same when suddenly a speeding truck bearing no.RJ-01GA-9045 jumped the traffic signal which was red on his side and hit into the motorcycle, resulting in injuries to the occupants of the motorcycle. He deposed that the driver of the truck was rash to the extent that he did not stop the truck even after hitting the motorcycle and crushed one of the occupants namely Gautam Kumar causing his death on the spot. He further deposed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending truck. PW2 was duly cross examined by learned counsel of respondent no.2/insurance company. 9. No evidence was led on behalf of respondents. MACT no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. Contributory negligence 17. Respondent no.1 MACT no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Page no. 8 of 23 ss has neither cross examined PW-2 nor led any evidence to prove the contrary. Reliance is placed upon decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sudheer Kumar Rana vs. Surinder Singh (2008) 12 SCC 436, which held as under:- "9. If a person drives a vehicle without a licence, he commits an offence. The same, by itself, in our opinion, may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident. It has been held by the courts below that it was the driver of the mini truck who was driving rashly and negligently. If he was not driving rashly and negligently which contributed to the accident, we fail to see as to how, only because he was not having a licence, he would be held to be guilty of contributory negligence." Similar view was taken in Mohd. Siddiqui vs. National Insurance company Ltd. AIR 2020 SC 520 wherein it was held that a pillion rider, even if accompanied by more than the legally permitted numbers of passengers, does not automatically imply contributory negligence. For such a finding, it must be demonstrated that the pillion rider's action directly contributed to the occurrence of the accident or exacerbated its impact. The court emphasis that a violation of traffic laws, such as exceeding MACT no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Page no. 9 of 23 ss the permissible number of riders on a motorcycle, does not by itself establish contributory negligence. There must be a clear causal connection between the violation and the accident. Hence, no contributory negligence is made out on the part of the victim. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in MACT no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Page no. 10 of 23 ss Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 21. Page no. 11 of 23 ss (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability; (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 21.1. 21.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) MACT no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Page no. 12 of 23 ss and (vi)--involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 21.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability Abhishek vs Gopal Singh Rawat on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149378006/ 7 --Item (ii) (a). 21.7. As such, his functional disability is assessed to be same as assessed by the Medical Board i.e. 55%. For purpose of calculating loss of future income (since Sarla Verma judgment is silent on multiplier applicable in cases where the victim is below age of 15 years), as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Reshma Kumari & Ors.v. Madan Mohan (2013) 9 SCC 65, a multiplier of 15 would apply. Hence, compensation towards loss of MACT no.768/2018 Abhishek & anr. vs. Gopal Singh Rawat & ors. Page no. 14 of 23 ss future income is assessed to Rs.7,401/- (monthly income as per minimum wages Abhishek vs Gopal Singh Rawat on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149378006/ 8 of an unskilled worker) X 12 (annual computation) X 15 (multiplier) + 40% of total income (as future prospect) =Rs.18,65,052/-. 55% of this amount would be Rs.10,25,779/-. 31.
